Project Overview

A portfolio solution scenario exploring how application-access requests can move through one connected catalog, approval, and fulfillment process.

02

Business Scenario

Employee application-access requests required manual coordination between employees, managers, application owners, and IT teams.

03

Requirements

  • Capture the employee, application, access level, and business justification in a structured request.
  • Route the request through manager and application-owner approval before IT fulfillment.
  • Make ownership and request status visible throughout the process.

05

Solution Design

Design a ServiceNow catalog-based request process that captures the required access information and automatically routes the request through the appropriate approval and fulfillment stages.

06

Detailed Workflow / Architecture

The RITM exists before the approval flow begins. Either rejection stops fulfillment, records the decision, and notifies the requester; no SCTASK is created on that branch.

REQ → RITM → SCTASK

  1. REQsc_request

    The parent order. One REQ can contain multiple requested items; one item finishing does not mean every item in the order is complete.

  2. RITMsc_req_item

    The requested item. Its request reference links to the REQ; variables, approvals, and the fulfillment flow belong to the item.

  3. SCTASKsc_task

    An actionable fulfillment task. Its request_item reference links to the RITM. An item may need zero, one, or multiple tasks.

08

Implementation Approach

  1. 01

    Capture the access request

    Define requested_for, application, access_level, and business_justification variables. A shared requester variable set can be reused where the same fields and rules apply across items.

  2. 02

    Separate form behavior from enforcement

    Use Catalog UI Policies for conditional visibility and mandatory fields. Catalog Client Scripts handle helpful field interactions. Validate the application and permitted access level again in server-side processing.

  3. 03

    Resolve approvers, then create work

    Trigger Flow Designer for the requested item. Resolve the requested-for employee's manager and the application's configured owner. Run two approval stages, then Create Catalog Task with the RITM reference and configured assignment group.

  4. 04

    Track fulfillment and close intentionally

    Wait for required tasks to finish, distinguish successful completion from cancellation or failure, and update the RITM accordingly. Use the configured request lifecycle to complete the REQ only when its other items are also resolved.

09

Technical Logic

Approval gates

Proceed only on an explicit approved result from both stages. Rejected, cancelled, timed-out, and missing-approver paths require different handling; none should silently authorize access.

Task ownership

Map the selected application to an active fulfillment group through configuration. Put the requested access and business justification on the task for the fulfiller; task creation does not itself grant access.

Notification events

Notify approvers when action is required, the requester on rejection or completion, and fulfillment teams when work is assigned. Avoid resending messages on unrelated record updates.

10

Technical Challenges & Decisions

Missing manager or owner

Route to controlled triage instead of auto-approving. Capture why the request is blocked so an administrator can correct ownership data.

Shared variable sets

Reuse common requester fields, but keep application-specific access options on the item. This limits the impact of changing one application's rules.

Prevent premature closure

A closed task may be incomplete rather than successful. Check the intended terminal result and all required tasks before setting the item to fulfilled.

11

Testing Approach

Proposed validation scenarios and expected results for an isolated ServiceNow test environment.

Both approvals granted
Exactly the intended fulfillment task is created against the RITM and assigned to the configured group.
Manager or owner rejects
No fulfillment task is created; the requester receives the rejection outcome.
Approver or group missing
Request is held for triage without granting or implying access.
One REQ, several RITMs
Completing one RITM does not prematurely close unfinished siblings.
Cancellation or failed task
Item state and notifications reflect the actual outcome rather than successful fulfillment.
12

Outcome

DESIGNED OUTCOME

A standardized request process with clearer ownership, automated approval routing, and improved request visibility.
